extracted.intended_audience: students (undergraduate/graduate) considering or enrolled in MIT Algebraic Topology I
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus for MIT's Algebraic Topology I course describing meeting times, prerequisites, topics, recommended textbooks, assignments/exams, and grading policy. Intended to inform prospective and enrolled students about course structure and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: 18.701 Algebra I or 18.703 Modern Algebra; and 18.901 Introduction to Topology. Familiarity with topological spaces, covering spaces, and the fundamental group will be assumed, as well as comfort with the structure of finitely generated modules over a PID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Description / Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a course on the singular homology of topological spaces. Topics include: Singular homology, CW complexes, Homological algebra, Cohomology, and Poincare duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are lots of textbooks that treat algebraic topology more or less at the level of this course. (Lists titles/authors: Bredon — Topology and Geometry; Davis & Kirk — Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology; Dold — Lectures on Algebraic Topology; Hatcher — Algebraic Topology; May — A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology; Munkres — Elements of Algebraic Topology; Shastri — Basic Algebraic Topology; Spanier — Algebraic Topology; Vick — Homology Theory: An Introduction to Algebraic Topology.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed book includes a short parenthetical note (e.g., 'Complete and geometric', 'Concise', 'Chatty', 'Meticulous', 'Verbose', 'Encyclopedic', 'Efficient') and ISBNs/preview links where available to help choose based on style and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments and Exams
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be 6 problems sets and a 40 minute oral exam during final exam week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem sets constitute the primary coursework; the final assessment is an oral exam lasting 40 minutes held during the final exam week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading policy / Weights
rubrics_metrics.description: The course grade will be based on homework assignments (75%) and a 40 minute oral exam (25%) during final exam week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homework carries the majority of the grade (three-quarters), with the oral final accounting for one-quarter.
